diorama.settings.title: Map settings
diorama.settings.gpu_baking.tooltip: Draws map tiles on the graphics card instead of the processor, so they appear sooner and the game uses less CPU. The first tiles are also drawn the old way and compared; if they differ, your graphics card is too slow or anything goes wrong, Diorama goes back to the processor by itself.
diorama.gpu_baking.failed: GPU baking didn't match on this graphics card, so Diorama is drawing the map on the processor again. The game log has the details.
diorama.map.dimension_button: Next dimension's map (hold Shift to reverse)
diorama.map.dimension_button_key: %s: next dimension's map (hold Shift to reverse)
diorama.map.facing_turn: Click to turn the map (Shift: the other way)
diorama.map.facing_walk: Walk around to map this side
diorama.settings.minimap_shown.tooltip: Shows the minimap on the screen.
diorama.settings.compass.tooltip: Puts N, S, W and E on the minimap's edges. The map always faces north.
diorama.settings.coordinates.tooltip: Shows your block coordinates under the minimap.
diorama.settings.biome.tooltip: Shows the biome you're in under the minimap.
diorama.settings.game_time.tooltip: Shows the time of day under the minimap, with or without the day number. It turns blue once it's dark enough to sleep. In the Nether and the End it's the Overworld's time.
diorama.settings.auto_caves.tooltip: When you're underground, the minimap and the map show the cave you're in instead of the surface above.
diorama.settings.prefer_surface.tooltip: Keep the surface view while only a roof is over your head, like in a house, and switch to caves once you're really below ground.
diorama.settings.legible_caves.tooltip: Shade caves by depth: ground further below you fades to dark slate, and the map shows your own cave instead of seeing through the rock. Off, it shows caves, mineshafts and lava in the rock below you.
diorama.settings.position.tooltip: Where the minimap sits on the screen. Drag it anywhere, or put it in a corner.
diorama.settings.corner.tooltip: Puts the minimap in the next corner of the screen.
diorama.settings.size.tooltip: How wide the minimap is. It shrinks to fit a small screen.
diorama.settings.enlarged.tooltip: How big the minimap gets with the Enlarge minimap key. Pick that key in Controls.
diorama.settings.enlarge_toggle.tooltip: Press the Enlarge minimap key once to enlarge the minimap and again to shrink it, instead of holding it.
diorama.settings.zoom.tooltip: How close the minimap is zoomed in. The zoom keys change it too.
diorama.settings.opacity.tooltip: How solid the minimap's map is. Lower it to see the game through it. The frame, icons and text stay solid.
diorama.settings.text_size.tooltip: How big the compass letters and the lines under the minimap are. The steps follow your GUI scale, so the letters stay sharp.
diorama.settings.players.tooltip: Shows other players on the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.radar_minimap.tooltip: Shows players, mobs and dropped items on the minimap. Turn this off to reduce lag near large groups of mobs.
diorama.settings.radar_map.tooltip: Shows players, mobs and dropped items on the fullscreen map.
diorama.settings.hostile.tooltip: Shows monsters, like zombies and creepers, on the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.neutral.tooltip: Shows mobs that only attack when provoked, like wolves, bees and endermen, on the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.passive.tooltip: Shows animals, villagers and other harmless mobs on the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.items.tooltip: Shows items lying on the ground as small dots on the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.range.tooltip: Players, mobs and dropped items farther above or below you than this are left off the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.chunk_grid.tooltip: Draws chunk borders on the map.
diorama.settings.slime_chunks.tooltip: Marks the chunks where slimes spawn on the map. Single player only, in the Overworld: it needs the world's seed.
diorama.settings.spawn_spots.tooltip: Marks blocks on the map where monsters can spawn: those dark even by day, or also those dark only at night.
diorama.settings.claims.tooltip: Where land claimed with FTB Chunks, Open Parties and Claims or MineColonies shows, in its owner's colour: on the fullscreen map, or on the minimap too.
diorama.settings.drawings.tooltip: Where what you draw on the map shows: on the fullscreen map, or on the minimap too (lines and areas; notes stay on the fullscreen map).
diorama.settings.world_border.tooltip: The game's world border on the map, where a server has set one: a line on the ground in the colour of the border's wall, blue, or green while it grows and red while it shrinks. On the fullscreen map, or on the minimap too.
diorama.settings.web_map.tooltip: Shows your map in a web browser, for a second screen, with your arrow moving on it. This computer: only browsers on this computer can open it. My network: phones, tablets and other devices on your network can open it too, so anyone on that network can see your map and where you are. Chat shows the address when you join a world.
diorama.web_map.no_port: The web map couldn't start: ports %s to %s are all in use.
diorama.settings.waypoints_map.tooltip: Shows your waypoints on the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.waypoints_world.tooltip: Shows your waypoints in the world, with their distance, even through terrain.
diorama.settings.deaths.tooltip: Adds a waypoint where you die.
diorama.settings.deaths_reached.tooltip: Removes a death marker once you're back within 4 blocks of it.
diorama.settings.beds.tooltip: Puts a pin on the bed you last slept in.
diorama.settings.portals.tooltip: Puts a pin on every lit Nether portal, End portal and End gateway the map finds, and on a stronghold's End portal once you reach it.
diorama.settings.map_add_waypoints.toolt: Right-clicking the map offers Add waypoint here and Add temporary waypoint. Off, waypoints are added with their key or from the waypoint list.
diorama.settings.map_waypoints_button.to: The Waypoints button at the top of the map. Off, its key still opens the waypoint list.
diorama.settings.map_settings_button.too: The Settings button at the top of the map. Off, open settings from the mod list, or bind its key in Controls and press it while playing.
diorama.settings.map_maps_button.tooltip: The Maps button at the top of the map, where each dimension's maps are made and switched.
diorama.settings.map_coordinates.tooltip: The coordinates of the spot under the mouse on the map. Off, its tooltip still tells you the biome and how far away the spot is.
diorama.settings.map_dimension_button.to: The square at the bottom left of the map that shows another dimension's map without going there. It shows up once a second dimension has been mapped. Off, its key still works if you bind one.
diorama.settings.outlines.tooltip: Darkens the edge where a block stands in front of lower ground, so cliffs and roofs stand out.
diorama.settings.day_night.tooltip: How dark the map is drawn. With World time it gets dark at night as the game does, and torches, lamps and lava light it up. Caves and the Nether don't change.
diorama.settings.rounded_fog.tooltip: Rounds off the edge of the explored map, instead of following the square edges of chunks.
diorama.settings.fog_of_war.tooltip: Cave maps show only the blocks you've seen, even where the server allows the full map.
diorama.settings.server_note: Greyed out: set by this server
diorama.settings.server_set: This server sets this while you're on it. Your own setting comes back when you leave.
diorama.settings.server_set_file: Set in config/diorama-server.properties, which a modpack can ship.
diorama.settings.saved_chunks.tooltip: Singleplayer: draws every finished chunk in the world's save on the map, including areas made by tools like Chunky, without walking there. On a server with Diorama: draws the land other players explored, in your own resource pack. Only the main map, and caves stay hidden. What's already drawn stays when you turn this off.
diorama.settings.quality.tooltip: Fast fills in the map about four times sooner and draws simpler fog. For slower computers.
diorama.settings.type_outline.tooltip: Outlines mob heads in red, yellow or green for hostile, neutral or passive. Off, they're outlined in black.
diorama.settings.height_arrows.tooltip: Shows a small arrow beside players and mobs that are well above or below you. Off, they only fade.
diorama.settings.player_names.tooltip: Where other players' names show under their heads.
diorama.settings.radar_categories.toolti: Each kind of mob has its own on/off, icon size and names, and you can make categories of your own from any mobs.
diorama.radar_categories.title: Radar categories
diorama.radar_categories.about: A mob in one of your own categories follows that category instead of Hostile, Neutral or Passive mobs.
diorama.radar_category.shown.tooltip: Shows this category on the minimap and the map.
diorama.radar_category.icon_size.tooltip: How big this category's icons are drawn. The first step follows Icon size on the Radar tab.
diorama.radar_category.names.tooltip: Where names show under this category's icons.
diorama.radar_category.mobs.tooltip: Pick the mobs in this category.
diorama.radar_mobs.title: Mobs in %s
diorama.settings.arrow_color.tooltip: The colour of your own arrow on the minimap and the map.
diorama.settings.waypoint_labels.tooltip: What shows under waypoints in the world: the distance, plus the name when you're close or looking at it, always, or never.
diorama.settings.waypoint_distance.toolt: Waypoints further away than this leave the world and the minimap; the map still shows them all. Deaths, temporary waypoints and your bed always show.
diorama.settings.waypoint_beams.tooltip: A beam of light standing on waypoints in the world, in the waypoint's colour, so you can see where to walk: on temporary waypoints and death markers, on every waypoint, or on none. A beam shows wherever its waypoint does, so the distance setting limits them too.
diorama.settings.waypoint_size_minimap.t: How big waypoints are drawn on the minimap. The steps follow your GUI scale, so the pixels stay sharp.
diorama.settings.waypoint_size_map.toolt: How big waypoints are drawn on the map. The steps follow your GUI scale, so the pixels stay sharp.
diorama.settings.waypoint_text_size.tool: How big the name and distance under waypoints in the world are. The steps follow your GUI scale, so the letters stay sharp.
diorama.settings.waypoint_size_world.too: How big waypoints are drawn in the world. The steps follow your GUI scale, so the pixels stay sharp.
diorama.settings.teleport_command.toolti: The command Diorama sends to teleport you, for servers with their own instead of /tp. {x}, {y} and {z} become the spot.
diorama.teleport_command.label: Command
diorama.position.title: Minimap position
diorama.position.help: Drag the minimap to move it. Press C to center it.
diorama.position.not_in_world: Join a world to drag the minimap.
diorama.folder.name: Folder name
diorama.folder.hint: Pick a waypoint's folder in its editor.

diorama.folder.empty: No waypoints in this folder yet
diorama.waypoint.folder_tooltip: The folder this waypoint is in. Click to pick another; make folders in the waypoint list.
diorama.settings.icon_size.tooltip: How big players and mobs are drawn on the minimap and the map.
diorama.folder.show_here.tooltip: While you're in the %2$s, %1$s waypoints show on the maps and in the world too, faded, at their matching %2$s coordinates. Lasts until you leave the world.
diorama.settings.frame.tooltip: The border around the minimap: the dark frame, a clean Minecraft edge, or none.
diorama.settings.shape.tooltip: Whether the minimap is a square or a circle.
diorama.settings.radar_style.tooltip: How players and mobs show: their heads as pixel art, faces in boxes framed by mob type, or plain coloured dots.

diorama.map_off.about: In a ticked dimension Diorama is off: no minimap, no map, no waypoints in the world, and nothing is mapped there.
